title: Checks for first-party imports that are only used for type annotations, but aren't defined in a type-checking block.
summary: Imports that are only used for type annotations add a performance overhead at runtime. For first-party imports, they can also contribute to import cycles. If an import is _only_ used in typing-only contexts, it can instead be imported conditionally under an if TYPE_CHECKING: block to minimize runtime overhead. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-type-checking and made it stable in 0.8.0.
message_templates: Move application import `{}` into a type-checking block

title: Checks for imports that are required at runtime but are only defined in type-checking blocks.
summary: The type-checking block is not executed at runtime, so if the only definition of a symbol is in a type-checking block, it will not be available at runtime. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-type-checking and made it stable in 0.8.0.
message_templates: Move import `{}` out of type-checking block. Import is used for more than type hinting.
Quote references to `{}`. Import is in a type-checking block.

title: Checks for an empty type-checking block.
summary: The type-checking block does not do anything and should be removed to avoid confusion. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-type-checking and made it stable in 0.8.0.

title: Checks for unquoted type expressions in typing.cast() calls.
summary: This rule helps enforce a consistent style across your codebase. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-type-checking and made it stable in 0.10.0.
message_templates: Add quotes to type expression in `typing.cast()`

title: Checks if PEP 613 explicit type aliases contain references to symbols that are not available at runtime.
summary: Referencing type-checking only symbols results in a NameError at runtime. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-type-checking and made it stable in 0.10.0.

title: Checks for unnecessary quotes in PEP 613 explicit type aliases and PEP 695 type statements.
summary: Unnecessary string forward references can lead to additional overhead in runtime libraries making use of type hints. They can also have bad interactions with other runtime uses like PEP 604 type unions. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-type-checking. It is in preview.

title: Checks for the presence of string literals in X | Y-style union types.
summary: PEP 604 introduced a new syntax for union type annotations based on the | operator. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-type-checking and made it stable in 0.8.0.
